answer.text: New shares being issued by the company
Existing shareholders such as promoters or large investors selling shares already allotted, with proceeds going to the offerors and no fresh issue or change in share capital

explanation.text: The Logic: OFS is the sale of existing shares already allotted to offerors such as promoters or large investors. The proceeds go to the offerors and there is no fresh issue and no increase in the issuer's share capital. It is treated as a secondary-market transaction conducted through the primary-market route. The Trap: New shares being issued describes an IPO or FPO fresh issue, not OFS. Bonus issues and dividends are separate corporate actions. Note: Keep the load-bearing point on existing shares and no fresh issuance; do not characterise OFS as a specific exchange mechanism unless the source page actually supports that wording.
